content.user_title: Diagnose Audience Resonance in Your Draft
content.value_statement: A finished draft can contain clear ideas yet fail to connect with its intended audience. This skill locates specific resonance gaps and recommends focused edits using communication theory.
actual_capabilities: Extract explicit and implicit claims and identify whether the central claim is clear, diluted, or missing.
Identify the intended audience and desired response, such as understanding, saving, sharing, or taking action.
Select one primary communication theory and add a supporting theory only when distinct textual evidence justifies it.
Rate the dominant resonance mechanism as effective, weak, or ineffective using quotations from the draft.
Recommend sentence-specific deletions, compression, strengthening, and passages to retain.
Propose a revised outline organized around one central claim.
limitations: Requires an existing draft or partial manuscript; complete rewrites and opening scripts are outside its stated scope.
Does not predict views, click rates, recommendations, completion rates, or commercial value.
Audience emotions and sharing tendencies remain text-based hypotheses, not verified audience responses.
Explaining why previously successful content spread is outside the primary deliverable.

use_cases.title: Clarify a creator script
use_cases.description: Locate vague audience references and competing claims in an existing video script, then prioritize concrete revisions.

use_cases.title: Strengthen an educational article
use_cases.description: Check whether an article gives readers a clear practical use and identify sentences that need stronger explanations.

use_cases.title: Focus an organizational message
use_cases.description: Review whether an internal draft connects employee concerns to one central claim and a clear intended action.

prompt_templates.title: Review a first draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this draft for audience resonance: [draft]. Identify the central claim, quote the weakest passages, and suggest specific edits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing draft.

prompt_templates.title: Check audience fit
prompt_templates.prompt: My audience is [audience], and I want them to [action]. Diagnose this draft: [draft]. Flag vague identity references and missing practical value.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review with an explicit audience and desired response.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose the dominant mechanism
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [draft] for [audience]. Select one primary theory, quote supporting evidence, rate the mechanism, and explain missing conditions without predicting platform results.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a structured revision
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [draft] for [audience] seeking [action]. List claims and justify one primary theory. Provide deletion, compression, strengthening, retention, and one revised outline.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a draft with competing claims.

output_examples.input: Audience: first-time team leads. Draft: Everyone should communicate better. Good leaders are confident. Before assigning work, agree on the deadline and expected result.
output: Core issue: Broad advice obscures a useful action for first-time team leads.
Central claim: Agree on deadlines and expected results before assigning work.
Primary theory: Uses and gratifications. Practical usefulness is weak because generic claims delay the actionable guidance.
Delete: 'Good leaders are confident.' It introduces a separate claim without support.
Strengthen: Replace 'Everyone' with a concrete situation involving first-time team leads.
Retain: The final sentence. Revised outline: assignment confusion, agreement on expectations, one practical example.

output_examples.input: Audience: new freelancers. Draft: Late payments are frustrating. Clients are difficult. You should manage your business professionally.
output: Core issue: The draft names frustration without explaining its cause or giving readers control.
Central claim: Unclear payment expectations can leave new freelancers uncertain about their next step.
Primary theory: Emotional appraisal. The mechanism is weak because responsibility and control remain unspecified.
Delete or qualify: 'Clients are difficult.' The draft provides no evidence for this generalization.
Strengthen: Describe a specific unpaid invoice and clarify what action the freelancer can take.
Revised outline: concrete payment problem, its effect on planning, one actionable response.

best_practices: Provide the complete draft, intended audience, and one desired audience response.
Require quotations for each diagnosis and keep one primary theory unless separate evidence supports another.
Apply focused edits first, then validate audience response through real feedback rather than assumed platform outcomes.
anti_patterns: Requesting guaranteed virality, platform metrics, or commercial forecasts from a text diagnosis.
Submitting only a topic and expecting a complete article or opening script.
Adding emotional pressure or sharing triggers when the draft only needs to support understanding or saving.

faq.question: What should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide an existing draft or partial manuscript, its intended audience, and the response you want from readers.

faq.question: Will it rewrite the entire draft?
faq.answer: No. Its stated deliverables are diagnosis, specific editing actions, and a revised outline, not a finished replacement manuscript.

faq.question: Can it predict whether my content will go viral?
faq.answer: No. It examines textual mechanisms and explicitly excludes platform metric predictions and guarantees of popularity.

faq.question: Which theories can guide the review?
faq.answer: Options include social identity, framing, emotional appraisal, uses and gratifications, and online sharing. The review selects one primary theory.

faq.question: Does the skill require network access or shell commands?
faq.answer: The reviewed files contain editorial instructions and interface metadata. They do not require network requests or shell execution.

faq.question: Can it explain why an already published post succeeded?
faq.answer: That is outside its primary scope. It focuses on revising existing drafts rather than explaining proven distribution outcomes.
